answer: Pay storage agents per byte that survives random retrieval tests, not per account. Each registered sector must hold a slow, identity-specific encoding; a public registry rejects reuse of its commitment. If cedar divides into onyx and sparrow accounts, both need separate encoded replicas and must answer unpredictable probes before a deadline too short to rebuild them. Splitting names earns nothing without more disk space. Encoding and retrieval must be audited, or one stored copy could masquerade as many.
